To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
we developed a new method that can be used to deconvolute overlapping fragments and extract the local exchange data, which is particularly important in the case when the exchange is correlated.
a new algorithm based a maximum entropy principle can extract local hydrogen exchange data form overlapping fragments and can subtract the background due to natural isotopes and exchange buffer.

we developed a new algorithm for the deconvolution of overlapping isotopic distributions of protein fragment ions, which is particularly useful when the resolving power is not sufficient to resolve individual isotopic peaks and when isotopic distributions are complex and cannot easily be described with a simple binomial model.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the development and testing of a new computational algorithm, which allows for extraction of exchange data for individual segments from the isotopic patterns of overlapping fragments, and is capable of dealing with the complex isotopic distributions of correlated or semicorellated exchange.

the development and testing of a novel deconvolution algorithm for the analysis of HDX CAD MS data and the application of the method to the analysis of HD exchange in the native state of proteins as well as to the study of non-native protein conformations in solution.
the development of algorithms that allow to extract information about protein structure and dynamics from HDX CAD measurements.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the new algorithm is a powerful and versatile tool for the analysis of HDX CAD MS data.
the new algorithm is a valuable addition to the toolbox of HDX CAD MS and can be applied in many cases when the exchange data are obscured by the presence of natural and residual deuterons.
this paper describes a new algorithm to deconvolute isotopic distributions of protein fragments measured by HDX CAD MS.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the algorithm presented here is capable of solving a variety of HDX problems, which were previously considered to be difficult or impossible to address.
the new method can be used to extract local exchange data for any protein fragment, even in cases where the resolving power of mass analyzers is not high enough to avoid signal interference.
we have developed a method to extract local HDX data from the isotope distribution data of overlapping fragments, and we demonstrated the usefulness of the method by applying it to a set of proteins.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the problem of deconvolution can be solved in many cases, which makes HDX MS an extremely powerful tool for structural characterization of proteins.

the maximum entropy principle can be used to deconvolute complex isotopic distributions of peptide ions and extract local deuterium exchange data, even when the exchange in the protein is correlated or semicoorrelated.

the problem of extracting local exchange information from HDX CAD measurements can be solved by a straightforward deconvolution of the observed isotopic distributions, provided that the deconvolution is performed using a maximum entropy approach.
